name: The Standard Mascot VHS Slip
description: A slightly dusty, but reliably excellent viewing experience. Contains generalized family entertainment fun that everyone has enjoyed since the dawn of time.

name: Mascot II VHS Slip
description: A reliable staple for the collection. Perhaps a bit less exciting than the standard issue, but perfectly fine for filling out your shelves.

name: Mascot III VHS Slip
description: Good for casual viewing parties. We're still figuring out the exact plot points, but pure fun is guaranteed.

name: Mascot IV VHS Slip
description: A slightly more niche collection. Perfect for experienced collectors who appreciate the subtle cinematic artistry.

name: Ghostbusters (Original Rip)
description: It's out there! An old tape that captures the raw energy of supernatural investigation. Warning: May induce deep paranoia regarding household appliance noises.

name: The Grinch Who Stole Christmas (VHS Cut)
description: A surprisingly emotional cinematic experience! Don't let the seasonal joy fool you; this tape details a highly necessary anti-sentimentality protest. Perfect for non-believers.

name: Indiana Jones: Raiders of the Lost Ark (Bogus Rip)
description: A classic adventure! You can almost smell the stale jungle sweat and slightly burnt popcorn when you put this in. Contains thrilling action sequences!

name: Iron Man: Assembly Line Bloopers (Director's Cut)
description: It wasn't all super fights. This rip focuses on the delightful behind-the-scenes chaos—including slightly embarrassing casual sparring moments.

name: Movie Title Unknown: The Wild West Standoff
description: Pure dusty adrenaline. We are still negotiating the title, but we're pretty sure it involves shootouts, regrettable outfits, and questionable saloon piano music.

name: The Noble Vampire's Misadventures (Cape One)
description: Beware! It involves excessive melodrama and questionable gothic fashion. Contains extensive scenes of dramatic gazing into Venetian mirrors.

name: A Guide to Obscure Lore (GUID Title)
description: An esoteric document. We believe it's related to powerful magic, but honestly, the plot kept skipping sections, making it perfect for fan theories.

name: Forest Gump: Life's Quirks (Extended Cut)
description: A heartwarming, if historically inaccurate, journey through time. Proof that simplicity is often the ultimate cinematic power.

name: Frankenstein's Monster: Too Much Science
description: Ah yes, the predictable 'mad scientist unleashes creature' trope. Required viewing for any film enthusiast who enjoys existential dread and bad wigs.

name: The Ring's Shadow: Gandalf's Journey (Early Draft)
description: We thought this was lost pirate treasure! It’s epic, it's wise, and it might just contain crucial plot holes that we can fill in ourselves.

name: Gemini: The Bronze Standard (6NX)
description: A controversial, yet critically acclaimed look at the true power of lukewarm ambition. This version was deemed 'legally required viewing' despite its low production value.

name: Jedi Mind Games: The Council's Oversight (Unauthorized Rip)
description: High-stakes action! Contains dazzling lightsaber sequences and a deep philosophical discussion that absolutely no one understands, but sounds profound.

name: The Joker: Smile Now (Boarding Pass Edition)
description: A perfect blend of anarchy and questionable performance art. We advise viewing this alone, ideally while wearing gloves.

name: Karate Kid: All Through the Years (Dojo Dropout Edit)
description: A highly dramatic rewatch of fundamental physical comedy. Excellent for those who still believe in the transformative power of a decent gi.

name: The Matrix: Choosing Your Reality (Select Cuts)
description: Will you know the truth? Or would it simply be easier to just watch this again? Contains excellent slow-motion wire work.

name: The Curse of the Pharaoh's Slapstick (Mummy Tape)
description: Less actual curses, more elaborate traps! An oddly entertaining look at ancient burial practices mixed with terrible practical jokes.

name: Ogre Mania: Cave Dweller Comedy
description: You think they are scary? Wait until you see the blooper reels. A low-budget, high-concept journey into monstrous misunderstanding.

name: Pan: The God of Forgotten Picnic Spots
description: A surprisingly sweet look at nature's whimsy. Perfect counterpoint to the cynical nihilism of other reels.

name: The Pirate's Lost Loot (Overly Romantic Rip)
description: Adventure! Swashbuckling! And a baffling amount of focus on romantic interludes compared to the actual treasure mapping. Keep an eye out for authentic brine stains.

name: Austin Powers: Licensed Bad Taste Experience
description: Pure, unadulterated groovy shag carpet disco chaos. Requires a strong appreciation for ill-fitting suits and questionable spy gadgetry.

name: Rambo: Single Shot Survival Tactics (The 'Training' Version)
description: It’s about more than just a big gun. It's about the *spirit* of self-reliance, and possibly some minor violations of international law.

name: Rocky II: The Gloves and the Grunt (Training Montage Extended)
description: The definition of persistence. A cinematic masterpiece about hitting things with your fists, preferably in a well-lit gym.

name: Sith Lords: Ethical Grievances (Dark Side Commentary)
description: A meta take on questionable villain motivation. Highly rated by dramatic aficionados who prefer their evil to be moody.

name: The Terminator: Time Travel Triumphant (Initial Draft)
description: A relentless chase sequence that transcends time. Contains a lot of industrial grit and the unsettling realization that you probably should have stayed home.

name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: sewer Life (Educational Rip)
description: Surprisingly insightful look into urban plumbing and martial arts. A genuinely bizarre, but highly collectible piece of media.

name: The Classic Vampire Cape No. 1
description: A bit much melodrama and far too comfortable for seasonal viewing.

name: The Man Who Got Away: Will Wallace (Test Footage)
description: A highly enigmatic collection of footage. Is it a man? Is it memory? We don't know, which is probably what makes it priceless.
